findings.title: NPE when the 'Clients' type resource is missing
findings.body: When no resource exists for the client, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is used as the fallback. That method returns null if the schema is unsupported or no `Clients` resource exists, but the result is passed straight to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. That call dereferences the resource and throws an NPE. The case is realistic. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialised before this change never get the new `Clients` resource or the `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` and `map-roles-composite` scopes. For those realms every non-realm-admin client permission check becomes a 500 instead of a deny. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return client ids
findings.body: The method iterates `findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. Only the all-clients resource has type `Clients`, because `init()` sets it. Its name is the literal string `Clients`, not a client id. Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(...)` without `setType`, so `findByType` does not return them. The result is therefore either `{"Clients"}` or an empty set, never the ids of the clients the caller can access. Anything relying on this method for filtering gets wrong results. The method is also not covered by any test.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `Users`: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username otherwise. For `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. That is null for both the all-clients resource and per-client resources, whose name is the client UUID. Listing the resources of a Clients permission therefore returns resources with a null name, so the API and UI cannot show 'All clients' or the clientId. It should return something like 'All clients' for the type resource and the clientId for per-client resources.

findings.title: V2 clients() throws UnsupportedOperationException from methods reachable at runtime
findings.body: `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns a `ClientPermissionsV2` whose `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions` and the `*Permission` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Before this change V2 used the V1 implementation, which simply returned false or an empty result. Code paths that still call these methods now produce a 500 instead of a normal deny or empty answer. Examples are the legacy token-exchange permission check (`canExchangeTo`) and `GET /clients/{id}/management/permissions`, which calls `isPermissionsEnabled`. The V2 implementation should return safe values (false, empty, or a proper 4xx) rather than throwing from request paths.

findings.title: Cleanup listener is skipped under V2, leaving orphan client resources and permissions
findings.body: The removal listener is now wrapped in `isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1). V1 and V2 are mutually exclusive versions of the feature, so the listener does nothing under V2. The wrapper is needed because `setPermissionsEnabled` now throws in V2. However, nothing replaces the cleanup. When a client is deleted, the per-client resource named by its UUID, and any permission that references it, stays in the admin-permissions resource server. Stale resources are left behind and the permissions still refer to a nonexistent client. V2 needs its own removal handler that deletes the resource, or detaches it from the permissions.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods describes a return value
findings.body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are `void` methods that throw `ForbiddenException`. Their new Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if canView() returns true' and 'Returns {@code true} if canViewClientScopes() returns true'. The other `require*` methods correctly say 'Throws ForbiddenException if ...'. The wording is copy-pasted from the `can*` methods and misdescribes the contract.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared client and roles without cleanup, and key paths are untested
findings.body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles, a composite and a role mapping. None of this is restored or registered with `realm.cleanup()`, and `onAfter` removes only the permissions. State leaks between tests in the class, so results depend on test order. There is also no coverage for several paths added in this PR. `getClientsWithPermission` is untested. `map-roles-client-scope` is untested. The view-all-clients case with MANAGE or CONFIGURE implying VIEW is untested. Deleting a client that has permissions is untested. No negative case checks that a per-client permission on client A does not grant access to client B beyond the one 'can't update a different client' assertion.
